The reply says the sources conflict and calls the matter "Unresolved," but it also says the 290 km figure is "slightly better supported." That leans toward B without firmly committing, and the stated confidence of 35 is low. The question is whether this counts as picking B.

The reply opens by declaring the question unresolved, which points toward N. Yet it does name 290 km as better supported, which is a lean toward B. The classification rule says to choose B when the reply gives B as its answer, even with caveats. Here the reply does not give an answer outright. It says the matter is unresolved and only notes a slight preference in support. A slight preference expressed within an "unresolved" verdict is a hedge, not a commitment.

Still, "slightly better supported" does express a preference for B. The N criteria include presenting both "without preferring either," and this reply does prefer one. The preference is weak, but it is stated, so I lean toward B.
